TL;DR
TEE-el-DEE-ar
interjection / noun (Millennial slang)
Initialism for too long; didn’t read, from early-2000s internet forums and Usenet, first as a dismissive reply to a long post, then as a label for a summary placed at the top or bottom of one ("TL;DR: the meeting is moved to Friday"). Reddit made the summary use standard in the 2010s, and dictionaries noted the term by about 2013. Variants: tl;dr, TLDR.

Definition · Webster 1828 · Scriptures · Corruption · Roots · Usage · Related

Biblical Definition

TL;DR means "too long; didn’t read." It began as a brush-off to anyone who wrote more than a screenful, and it became a helpful convention: the one-line summary at the top of a long post. The Christian observation: both uses deserve attention. The summary is a real service, and Scripture loves brevity. "In the multitude of words there wanteth not sin: but he that refraineth his lips is wise" (Pro 10:19). "Let thy words be few" (Ecc 5:2). The Lord Jesus summarized the whole law in two commandments (Mat 22:37-40), the greatest TL;DR ever given. But the dismissive use reveals a cultural problem that matters for Christians: shrinking attention. A generation trained on short posts finds long reading hard, and the Bible is long. Its deepest treasures require sustained attention. When Ezra read the Law to the people, "he read therein … from the morning until midday … and the ears of all the people were attentive unto the book of the law" (Neh 8:3). The blessed man’s "delight is in the law of the LORD; and in his law doth he meditate day and night" (Psa 1:2). The Bereans "searched the scriptures daily" (Act 17:11). A Christian cannot live on summaries of God’s Word. A father teaches his children to write clearly and briefly, to read slowly and deeply, and to treat the Bible as the one book that is never TL;DR, because every word of it is breath from God.

Webster 1828 Definition

Millennial internet initialism (early 2000s; Reddit summaries 2010s) for too long; didn’t read; brevity is biblical (Ecc 5:2), but shrinking attention threatens the deep reading Scripture requires (Neh 8:3; Psa 1:2).

TL;DR, interj. / n. (Millennial internet slang, early 2000s–present; initialism of too long; didn’t read) (1) A dismissive reply to a long text. (2) A brief summary of a longer text. Also TLDR.

Webster (1828), root read: READ, verb transitive The preterit and participle passive read is pronounced red. [Gr. to say or tell, to flow; a speaker, a rhetorician. The primary sense of read is to speak, to utter, that is, to push, drive or advance. This is also the primary sense of ready, that is, prompt or advancing, quick. Latin gratia, the primary sense of which is prompt to favor, advancing towards, free. The elements of these words are the same as those of ride and Latin gradior, etc. […]

Decode for parents: teach clear summaries and long attention; the Bible needs the second.

Key Scripture

Pro 10:19 — "In the multitude of words there wanteth not sin: but he that refraineth his lips is wise."

Ecc 5:2 — "Be not rash with thy mouth, and let not thine heart be hasty to utter any thing before God: for God is in heaven, and thou upon earth: therefore let thy words be few."

Mat 22:37-40 — "Jesus said unto him, Thou shalt love the Lord thy God with all thy heart, and with all thy soul, and with all thy mind. This is the first and great commandment. And the second is like unto it, Thou shalt love thy neighbour as thyself. On these two commandments hang all the law and the prophets."

Neh 8:3 — "And he read therein before the street that was before the water gate from the morning until midday, before the men and the women, and those that could understand; and the ears of all the people were attentive unto the book of the law."

Psa 1:2 — "But his delight is in the law of the LORD; and in his law doth he meditate day and night."

Modern Corruption

TL;DR rightly prizes brevity, but its dismissive form signals shrinking attention, which starves the deep, daily reading that Scripture asks of believers.

expand to see more

The corruption is attention trained for scraps. The digital world rewards the short, the punchy, and the summarized, and many young people now struggle to read anything long. That is not a neutral change for Christians, who are people of a long Book, written with genealogies, laws, poems, letters, and prophecies that unfold only to patient readers. A faith fed only on verse-of-the-day snippets will be thin.

The recovery is the discipline of deep reading. Read whole books of the Bible aloud as a family; memorize passages, not only verses; read good long books. Ezra’s congregation stood for half a day to hear the Law, and they wept and rejoiced. Teach the young to summarize well for others, and to refuse summaries of the Word of God for themselves.

Greek & Hebrew Roots

Old English raedan (to advise, interpret, read) → read → early-2000s forums TL;DR → 2010s Reddit summary label → dictionaries c. 2013.
